messages:
Maya Patel: Heads up — HelixCare procurement just sent a vendor questionnaire tying together DPA + PCI scoping questions. They specifically asked for: encryption at rest details, customer-managed KMS options, audit log retention, and proof of SOC2 scope. Need answers back by Fri EOD or they’ll push the PO. Copy of key Qs pasted below.

Jordan Kim: Thanks Maya. Do we want to use the standard DPA bundle + our PCI-approved wording? Who's owning the reply?

Liam O'Neil: I can own the helixcare thread and send the initial responses. Will need security-approved phrasing for the crypto/KMS bits. Also confirm EU data residency language.

Devon Chen: I can provide the security-approved wording. Draft below — feel free to reuse.

Devon Chen: ```Q: Is data encrypted at rest?
A: Yes. All customer data stored in Redwood-hosted environments is encrypted at rest using AES-256. For Hosted deployments we use provider-managed KMS; for Dedicated and Private deployments customers can opt for customer-managed keys (CMKs) via integrated KMS/HSM.```

Devon Chen: ```Q: What about encryption in transit?
A: TLS 1.3 is enforced for all in-flight connections. Mutual TLS is supported for Private deployments.```

Devon Chen: ```Q: Audit logs and retention?
A: Audit logs (access events, admin actions, key rotations) are retained for 90 days by default in Hosted, configurable up to 1 year for Dedicated/Private with enterprise add-on. We can provide export of relevant audit records during procurement review under NDA.```

Devon Chen: ```Q: SOC2 / scope?
A: Redwood maintains SOC2 Type II for our platform services. For Private deployments customers may operate within their own SOC2 scope; we provide documentation and evidence packages for integration.```

Maya Patel: That's great — concise and procurement-friendly. Liam, can you paste these into a single reply and add a one-line note about support for on-prem (air-gapped) deployments?

Liam O'Neil: On it. Quick Q: For the audit export sentence, is it safe to offer sample logs under NDA?

Devon Chen: Yes — safe. We redact sensitive tokens; we provide schema + example events. Add: "redacted sample events available under NDA."

Liam O'Neil: Got it. I'll draft and send in ~25m and tag @Jordan for sign-off on tone. Also flagging renewal risk: if PO slips more than 2 weeks we may need to escalate to AE.

OnboardBot: Task added: "Send compliance answers to HelixCare" assigned to Liam O'Neil, due 2025-11-07.

Jordan Kim: Excellent. Liam — if you want a hand with the procurement form fields (they sometimes use weird dropdowns), ping me and I’ll help paste.

Liam O'Neil: Sent draft to procurement + helixcare contact at 1768007801. Included the Devon wording and added: "We support customer-managed KMS for Private deployments; Hosted customers may request CMK support with an enterprise contract."

Maya Patel: Thank you — please paste HelixCare's initial response here once you get it. :thumbsup:

Liam O'Neil: HelixCare acknowledged at 1768007899 — they had one follow-up on tokenization of PII and asked if we offer field-level tokenization. I asked for specifics and said we'd confirm. Will loop in Devon if they want a product-level answer.

Devon Chen: For tokenization: we currently offer application-level tokenization patterns; for strict PCI tokenization we recommend using customer-managed HSM in Private deployments. I’ll prepare a short note to paste into thread.

Maya Patel: Perfect — thanks everyone. Keeping this as low-friction as possible keeps procurement moving and lowers renewal risk.
